questions.note: Order and cascade are right: the hallux is about 2 mm ahead of toe 2 and toes 3 to 5 descend. But toes 2-4 are near-identical parallel cylinders with deep clefts [D2], from below they are stalks, not pads [D3], the hallux stands off toe 2 [D4], toe 5 angles away in plan [D9] and has a step at its root [D6].

The lateral malleolus is lower and further back, with the hollow in front (V3), and the Achilles cord has hollows either side (V8): good, as in the scan. But from behind the medial ankle bulks out and the column leans [D1], in V2 the medial malleolus reads as dents, not a dome, no anterior ankle crease reads, and the back outline has a notch at z 110 [D7].

defects.what: From behind, the leg column above the heel leans medially and its medial half is a broad shaded face out to x 1950, about 55 mm past the heel's medial edge (the scan's stays at that edge). The ankle reads as a flared trunk, not a column narrowing into the Achilles.
defects.fix: Keep the scan's ankle sections through z 95-125 and ease the leg's axis and width into them, so the medial outline rises from the malleolus at about the heel's width, as the scan's does.

defects.what: Toes 2-4 are straight, parallel, near-identical cylinders split by deep clefts that run back toward the webs. The nail sits on the very tip and no pulp bulges ahead of or under it, so they read as fingers (also in plan).
defects.fix: Shorter, plumper toes pressed together, the PIP knuckle slightly raised and the pulp bulging ahead of and below the nail, as in the scan and the anchor photos.

defects.what: From below, the lesser toes are narrow stalks with ring bands; the scan beside them shows round, plump pads behind a toe sulcus.
defects.fix: Domed plantar toe pads nearly as wide as each toe's base, one soft crease at each joint, sitting behind a continuous sulcus.

defects.what: The hallux and toe 2 stand apart: a see-through slit about 3 mm wide (about 10 px at 3.1 px/mm) runs along their distal 35 mm in plan, and again in the V4o silhouette, although the declaration says the hallux touches toe 2.
defects.fix: Close the hallux onto toe 2 so their sides meet along the distal phalanges, as in the scan.

defects.what: The extensor tendons are long, even, sharp-edged cords running from the front of the ankle onto the toes, the crispest relief on the foot (also V3, plan, V5f); they read as cables laid on the dome.
defects.fix: Low (1 mm or less), broad, soft-shouldered ridges that fade distally into the dorsum, with the EHL the only distinct one at rest.

defects.what: Toe 5 meets the forefoot through a crisp step all round near its root, with a second ring just ahead of it, like a tube pushed into a sleeve.
defects.fix: Run toe 5's skin smoothly into the lateral forefoot, its base widening into the 5th MT head with no edge.

defects.what: A small notch breaks the back outline at about z 110, where the model's leg meets the scan's: the back of the leg above sits about 5 mm forward of the scan's line below.
defects.fix: One smooth curve from the Achilles into the heel's prominence, with the blend matched to the scan's back line at the cut.

defects.what: Small dark ticks sit at the roots of the 2-3 and 3-4 webs.
defects.fix: Close the webs as soft U-shaped folds with no pinch.

defects.what: In plan the 5th toe stands apart and angles away from the 4th across an open cleft.
defects.fix: Curl it, roll it 30-45 degrees onto its lateral side and tuck it against the underside of the 4th.

ranked: [D1] From behind (V8), the ankle is wrong: the column above the heel leans medially and its medial half fans out to about 55 mm past the heel's medial edge. A real ankle from behind narrows into the Achilles over a heel about as wide, as the scan beside it does.

[D2] Toes 2-4 still read as fingers: straight, parallel cylinders of near-identical shape, deep clefts back toward the webs, the nails at the very tips and no pulp bulging ahead. A man's lesser toes are short, plump and pressed together, the PIP knuckle raised.

[D5] The extensor tendons are long, even, sharp-edged cords from the ankle onto the toes, the crispest relief on the foot. A lean man's tendons are low, soft ridges that fade into the dome, sharp only with the toes lifted.
[D3] From below (V4) the lesser toes are narrow stalks with ring bands; the scan beside them shows the real thing, round plump pads behind a toe sulcus, nearly as wide as the toes' bases.

[D4] The hallux and toe 2 do not touch: a see-through slit about 3 mm wide runs along their distal 35 mm in plan and in the V4o silhouette, where the declaration and the scan have them lying together.
[D9] In plan the 5th toe stands apart and angles away from the 4th with an open cleft; a booted man's 5th toe is curled, rolled onto its side and tucked against or under the 4th.

In V2 the medial malleolus reads as two dark dents around a faint swell, not the broad round dome that is the main landmark of a lean man's medial ankle. The scan shares this, but the medial malleolus still does not read as the higher, rounder one.
[D7] The V2o silhouette has a notch in the Achilles line at about z 110, where the model's leg meets the scan's; the real back outline is one smooth curve from the calf into the heel.
[D6] Toe 5 meets the foot through a crisp step all round in V3, like a tube in a sleeve; real toes run into the forefoot with no edge.
No anterior ankle crease reads at the front of the ankle in V1f, V2 or V3; the one horizontal line across the dorsum in V1f is the venous arch, well forward of the crease line.
Declared out of scope, but it hides the scope: the veins are tall, uniform raised tubes and the venous arch crosses the dorsum like a strap, so in V1f, V2 and plan the dorsum's dome is hard to judge.
The plan's cut cap at z 125 shows a crease across its medial half and a hard corner, unlike the scan's flat oval; it may be the same fold as the medial bulk behind the ankle in V8.
[D8] Small dark ticks sit at the roots of the 2-3 and 3-4 webs in V5f.
Seen whole, the foot proper (heel bell, sole with its pads and lateral band, arch, plan outline, side profiles) now reads as a real foot; what gives it away is the toes and the ankle-to-leg blend.
